name: Familial Cortical Myoclonic Tremor with Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Cortical Myoclonic Tremor with Epilepsy

criteria.description: Presence of adult-onset cortical myoclonic tremor confirmed by electrophysiological studies
History of adult-onset epilepsy with generalized or focal seizures
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing cortical reflex myoclonus and epileptiform discharges
Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (cortical myoclonic tremor, epilepsy history, and positive family history) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electrophysiological confirmation is important to differentiate from other myoclonic disorders

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by fine, irregular, high-frequency tremor with cortical origin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electrophysiological evidence of cortical reflex myoclonus
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by EEG and somatosensory evoked potentials

genetic: Mutations in genes such as CTNND2, ADRA2B (depending on subtype)
other: Electrophysiological studies showing cortical reflex myoclonus
EEG with generalized or focal epileptiform discharges

distinguishingFeatures: No cortical reflex myoclonus on electrophysiology
Typically no family history of epilepsy
Characteristic EEG pattern with 4-6 Hz polyspike and wave
Often associated with metabolic or storage disorders

redFlags: Lack of family history in suspected cases
references: van Rootselaar AF, et al. Familial cortical myoclonic tremor with epilepsy: a review. Brain. 2005;128(3):571-582.
Matsumoto JY, et al. Electrophysiological features of familial cortical myoclonic tremor with epilepsy. Clin Neurophysiol. 2011;122(4):765-771.
